subject: Flexible burst credits and guardrails for Dedicated GPU pools
messages:
From: Ellie Park <ellie.park@atlashealth.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Pilot sizing question — burst capacity and procurement details

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Atlas Health is excited about the latency and cost profile you showed. A couple of procurement and architecture questions came up while we scoping the pilot:

- We want a Dedicated GPU pool for the pilot (approx 6-week run) with a target baseline throughput of ~120 requests/minute (75 token average) during business hours. What sizing do you recommend (GPU types / pool size) to achieve 99th p99 latency < 300ms?
- We expect occasional spikes during batch ingest and peak patient hours — how does Redwood handle burst above the reserved throughput? Specifically: burst headroom, maximum surge rate relative to baseline, cooldown windows, and how surcharges are applied.
- Procurement asked for an example commercial construct we can include in the SOW and a short description of any caps or guardrails (we'd like predictable bills).

Can you send a short options list (pool sizing, burst model, and an example monthly cost for a pilot + an annual committed SKU if we expand)? Procurement is on copy for next steps.

Thanks,
Ellie Park
Director of ML Integrations
Atlas Health

From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Ellie Park <ellie.park@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-10T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pilot sizing question — burst capacity and procurement details

Hi Ellie — great to meet you yesterday. Quick summary and three options that map to different risk/price tradeoffs. See inline for answers and an attached SOW template (SOW_MVP_pilot_v1.pdf).

1) Recommended baseline pool (low-latency):
- Suggested: 3 x A10-equivalent GPU instances in a shared Dedicated pool (can be mapped to Redwood's "medium" SKU)
- Expected baseline throughput: ~150 requests/minute, p99 < 300ms for 75-token responses with our runtime optimizations and prefix caching

2) Burst model options (how surplus capacity is handled):
A. Burst add-on (default):
- Headroom: up to +40% capacity over baseline for short windows
- Max surge: up to 2.0x baseline in exceptional cases (subject to pool availability)
- Cooldown: automatic cooldown of 10 minutes after sustained burst beyond headroom
- Pricing: billed as linear surcharge applied to token-equivalent usage during burst windows (example: 35% surcharge on token unit cost for burst usage)

B. Flexible burst credits (pre-purchased pool of credits):
- Headroom: effectively unlimited until credits are consumed (subject to overall infra limits)
- Cooldown: soft cooldowns (configurable) but credits allow sustained spikes without immediate throttling
- Pricing: one-time credit purchase (e.g., $X per 1M burst-token credits); credits are consumed at a defined rate per token during spikes

C. Reserved + emergency override (enterprise):
- Headroom: carved emergency capacity that can be enabled for incidents (manual/auto)
- Cooldown: shortened to 5 minutes for incident windows with an emergency surcharge and pre-approved SLA
- Pricing: higher reserved commit with lower unit costs plus a separate emergency surcharge band

3) Commercial examples (pilot):
- Pilot (6 weeks): Medium Dedicated pool (3x A10-eq) + Burst add-on (40% headroom)
  - Monthly equivalent (pro-rated): $18,500 for the reserved pool + estimated burst surcharges up to $2,500 (depends on spike volume)
- If Atlas moves to a 12-month committed reserved pool we can provide a tiered discount (see Karthik's note).

I looped Karthik and Neha for the discount & procurement specifics — Karthik will share the sliding discount and guardrail options, and Neha will attach the procurement questionnaire to get SOC/compliance items flowing.

Best,
Irene Choi
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Thanks Irene — adding commercial specifics so procurement can review. Below is a concrete pricing ladder and a proposed commercial guardrail we usually accept for production contracts. Quoting examples for a 3 GPU medium pool mapped to your pilot needs.

Pricing ladder (example):
- Month-to-month reserved pool (no annual commit): $18,500/month equivalent (no discount).
- 12-month commit: 15% discount on reserved pool -> $15,725/month equivalent.
- 24-month commit: 25% discount -> $13,875/month equivalent.

Burst/Autoscale add-on constructs: 
- Default burst add-on (metered surcharge): 35% surcharge on token-equivalent usage that exceeds baseline capacity during burst windows. Billed monthly as usage line item.
- Flexible burst credits: prepaid credit bucket: $1,100 per 1M burst-token credits (credits consumed only during burst windows). For pilots we can offer a one-time 25k credit for free (to cover initial spikes).
- Surge rate cap (customer-protected): standard is no explicit cap, but for enterprise deals we can offer a negotiated cap expressed as a percentage of monthly spend (e.g., 25% cap on monthly surge charges) with exceptions for security incidents or DDoS.

Guardrails and exceptions:
- Cooldown defaults: 10 minutes. We can shorten to 8 minutes for production SLAs, or to 5 minutes for emergency overrides with an elevated fee.
- Emergency override: manual enablement by your SRE with predefined thresholds — we propose including an "incident allowance" clause in the SOW.

I'll attach a redlineable pricing addendum and SOW language; Neha, please attach the procurement questionnaire and SOC2 link.

—Karthik
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference

Thanks — procurement here. A few items we need clarified before legal and finance will approve the pilot SOW: 

1) Surge charge predictability: Atlas requires a cap on surge charges for pilots and initial production. We request a hard cap set to 20% of monthly reserved spend for the pilot period (pilot = 6 weeks). Any usage above that cap should be treated as "notify and pre-approve" before being charged.
2) Cooldown windows: 10 minutes is fine for normal ops, but our SREs are requesting a 5-minute cooldown for low-latency endpoints in patient-facing flows. Is that configurable? If it shortens cost predictability we need an estimate of incremental cost.
3) Compliance deliverables: please provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and data flow diagrams. We attached our procurement questionnaire for Redwood to fill out.

Attached: Atlas_Procurement_Questionnaire.xlsx

Procurement Team
Atlas Health

Hi Atlas Procurement — thanks for the clear asks. Below are proposed compromises that align with our standard enterprise playbook and keep the pilot operationally simple. Quoting your points inline.

> 1) Surge charge predictability: Atlas requires a cap on surge charges for pilots and initial production. We request a hard cap set to 20% of monthly reserved spend for the pilot period (pilot = 6 weeks). Any usage above that cap should be treated as "notify and pre-approve" before being charged.

Proposed: We can accept a pilot cap of 25% of monthly reserved spend (pro-rated for 6 weeks) with the following exception: verified security incidents or DDoS are excluded from the cap and handled via our incident billing process. For larger committed deals (12+ months) we can move the cap to 20% and bake it into the pricing addendum.

> 2) Cooldown windows: 10 minutes is fine for normal ops, but our SREs are requesting a 5-minute cooldown for low-latency endpoints in patient-facing flows. Is that configurable? If it shortens cost predictability we need an estimate of incremental cost.

Proposed: We can configure an 8-minute default cooldown for production, and offer a configurable 5-minute emergency cooldown for agreed-upon endpoints. Example incremental cost: shortening cooldown from 10 -> 5 mins typically increases burst exposure by ~30% for sustained spike profiles; for your pilot that maps to an illustrative incremental surge cost of $1,200–$2,000 (pro-rated), depending on observed spike cadence. We'll include observability hooks so you can track burst consumption in the Console.

> 3) Compliance deliverables: please provide SOC 2 Type II attestation and data flow diagrams. We attached our procurement questionnaire for Redwood to fill out.

Attached: SOC2_Type2_Attestation.pdf (signed) and we've started filling the questionnaire — Neha will share the partially completed spreadsheet by EOD.

Next steps:
- We will update the SOW to include the 25% pilot cap and the 8/5 minute cooldown language and send a DocuSign link for the pilot SOW.
- Karthik will include the 25k burst credit and the 12-month discount language as optional expansion terms.

Thanks — we can jump on a 30-min call if you'd like to walk through the SOW and procurement questionnaire together.

Best,
